literal: Not enduring body and life will ride the palmyra horse, modesty having cast aside and put away.
translation: My body and life, unable to bear this suffering, will ride the palmyra horse, having completely cast aside and put away all modesty.
modern: துன்பத்தைப் பொறுக்க முடியாத என் உடலும் உயிரும், நாணத்தை நீக்கித் தூரத்தே வைத்துவிட்டு, மடலேறும்.
explanation: The lover expresses the extremity of his grief caused by separation from his beloved. He declares that his body and life can no longer endure the pain, forcing him to resort to 'madalēṟutal'—the public act of riding a horse made of rough palmyra stems to proclaim his love. To take this desperate step, he must completely cast aside ('nīkki') and put away ('niṟuttu') his sense of shame and modesty ('nāṇ'). The couplet illustrates how overwhelming love-sickness overpowers a person's natural restraint and social decorum.
